keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Poignant, bittersweet Australian alternative-rock ballad in D major rich with high ringing drone pedal tones
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor is the relative minor of D major

mainProgression.description: Bernard Fanning's emotional masterpiece: an intimate D to G pendulum during the verses that expands into the cathartic Bm - G - D - A chorus singalong.

sectionProgressions.description: Gentle acoustic fingerpicking keeping high D and A pedal tones ringing statically across both chords
Anthemic release ('It's coming round again...') launching into the relative minor Bm
Introspective supertonic minor breakdown building tension toward the final stadium chorus

harmonicFunction: D (I) - Grounded tonic providing solace and warm acoustic resonance
G (IV) - Subdominant chord creating a gentle, swaying acoustic cradle
Bm (vi) - Relative minor opening the chorus with profound melancholy and vulnerability
A (V) - Dominant resolution completing the chorus phrase with poignant finality
Em (ii) - Minor stepping stone deepening the emotional journey in the bridge

techniques.name: High Drone Pedal Point & Fingerstyle Acoustic
techniques.description: Anchoring fingers on the 3rd fret of strings 1 and 2 (D and A notes) while transitioning bass roots beneath

sequence: Keep the high D note ringing consistently on the 2nd string 3rd fret
Pluck bass root notes on downbeats (string 4 for D, string 6 for G, string 5 for Bm and A)
Follow with gentle arpeggiated finger plucks across the high strings
tips: Use the flesh of your thumb for the bass notes and index/middle for the treble strings
Avoid strumming too loudly during the verses to leave room for the vocal nuances
Add warm tube overdrive for the electric guitar tracks entering in the final chorus

techniques.name: Ian Haug Lyrical Electric Lead & Wide Vibrato
techniques.description: Singing melodic phrasing on the electric guitar, executing slow whole-step bends and wide vocal-like vibrato over the Bm - G - D - A progression

notes: Target D major chord tones: F# at fret 14 on string 1, D at fret 10/15 on string 1/2
Execute full whole-step bends at fret 14 (string 3) and fret 15 (string 2)
Slow, wide finger vibrato matching Bernard Fanning's vocal inflection
sequence: Begin with lyrical melody at the 10th and 14th frets on the high E string
Sustain the 15th-fret climax note with controlled, singing vibrato
Descend gracefully through the D major pentatonic scale into the open D chord resolution
tips: Support your fretting finger with two additional fingers when executing slow bends
Use a warm overdrive (Fulltone OCD or Blues Driver) with slight tape delay (350ms)
Focus on tone and touch rather than speed; every note should sing like a vocal line

sections.name: Intro Acoustic High-Drone Fingerpicking
sections.technique: High Drone Pedal Point & Fingerstyle Acoustic
sections.description: Bernard Fanning's intimate solo acoustic guitar picking the bittersweet D to G progression with ringing open high strings.
notes: Anchor your fingers on the 3rd fret of strings 1 and 2
Pluck the alternating bass notes cleanly with the thumb
Let the high treble strings ring together with warm acoustic sustain

sections.name: Verse 1 Bittersweet Pendulum
sections.technique: High Drone Pedal Point & Fingerstyle Acoustic
sections.description: Gentle acoustic strumming as Bernard Fanning delivers the iconic opening lines ('This life is short, baby that's a fact...').
notes: Play with delicate, controlled dynamics at 84 BPM
Smooth voice leading between open D and G major cowboy shapes
Keep the rhythm spacious and unhurried

sections.name: Chorus Singalong 'Coming Round Again'
sections.description: Full band burst into the legendary 'It's coming round again' chorus hook, with resonant acoustic and warm electric guitars.
notes: Open up the strumming with resonant full-chord strokes across all six strings
Lock into the slow, powerful 84 BPM pocket with John Collins's bass
Transition cleanly through the Bm barre chord at fret 2

sections.name: Bridge Minor Build
sections.description: Emotional dynamic build ('These days seem to fade so easily...') as the rhythm section swells and Ian Haug's electric guitar prepares the solo break.
notes: Build picking intensity gradually over the Em to G transition
Accent the downbeats on Bm and A
Crescendo to launch Ian Haug's soaring guitar solo

sections.name: Ian Haug's Soaring Electric Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Ian Haug Lyrical Electric Lead & Wide Vibrato
sections.description: Ian Haug's celebrated electric guitar solo. A masterclass in lyrical melodic phrasing and restraint: crying whole-step bends at the 14th fret of the G string and 15th fret of the B string, slow singing vibrato, and uplifting major pentatonic resolutions that capture the song's bittersweet nostalgia.
notes: Begin on the 10th fret of the high E string with singing melodic phrasing
Climb smoothly up to the 14th fret and sustain with wide finger vibrato
Hit the 15th-fret high note with emotional weight and slow, weeping release
Descend through the D major pentatonic scale to resolve gracefully back to the acoustic strumming

sections.name: Final Epic Chorus & Acoustic-Electric Outro
sections.description: Huge dual-guitar crescendo on the final chorus before stripping back to Bernard Fanning's solitary acoustic guitar ringing to the final chord.
sections.progression: Bm - G - D - A (repeating to final D)
notes: Combine heavy electric rhythm chording with acoustic dreadnought strumming
Ian Haug adds soaring 17th-fret fills over the vocal repetitions
Strip away the drums and electric guitars for a final tender strum on open D

guitar.recommended: Maton ECW80 Acoustic Dreadnought or Gibson J-45
alternatives: Gibson Les Paul Standard (Ian Haug electric leads)
guitar.pickup: Acoustic bridge piezo or mic'd acoustic dreadnought

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or Vox AC30 (clean chime)

effects.distortion: Fulltone OCD or Boss BD-2 Blues Driver for chorus electric crunch
effects.other: Analog Delay set to gentle quarter-note ambient repeats

beginner.title: Open Chords & Strumming Timing
steps: Learn open D, G, Bm (or Bm7 without barre), and A chords
Practice the slow, measured 84 BPM down-up strumming pattern
Memorize the verse D - G and chorus Bm - G - D - A forms
beginner.goals: Flawless transitions between the four chords at 84 BPM

intermediate.title: Fingerpicking & Pedal Drone Resonance
steps: Master the fingerpicked acoustic pattern on the verse
Keep the high D note ringing consistently on fret 3
Coordinate dynamic volume swelling between verse and chorus
intermediate.goals: Expressive acoustic touch with crystal-clear note separation

advanced.title: Electric Lead Layering & Outro Solo
steps: Learn Ian Haug's soaring electric counter-melodies in D major
Master the sustained whole-step bends and warm tube feedback
Blend acoustic rhythm and electric lead into a complete studio arrangement
advanced.goals: Stage-ready live performance of this modern Australian masterpiece

commonMistakes: Rushing the tempo: 84 BPM feels slow, so players frequently speed up during the chorus
Muting the high ringing drone strings with the palm or lazy fretting fingers
Playing the chorus barre chord (Bm) with too much tension
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 5 minutes of slow fingerpicking with a metronome at 84 BPM
Practice the Bm to G transition 10 times in isolation
Play along with the recording focusing on dynamic breath and emotional build
focusAreas: Ringing high drone strings throughout changes
Smooth volume transition from verse whisper to chorus explosion
metronomeWork: Set click to 84 BPM with 8th-note subdivisions
Practice counting the slow tempo to internalize the pocket
Ensure chord changes land precisely on beat 1 without rushing
